2.6.1.21.rationale: D-alanine:2-oxoglutarate aminotransferase (D-amino acid aminotransferase) is a standard PLP-dependent fold-type IV transaminase with a single catalytic activity; no literature reports a second fused catalytic domain.

2.6.1.5.rationale: Aromatic (phenylalanine) aminotransferase is a classic single-activity PLP transaminase; searches for bifunctional/multifunctional fusion returned no relevant hits.

2.6.1.58.rationale: L-phenylalanine:pyruvate aminotransferase is a single-activity aromatic aminotransferase with no reported second catalytic activity in the literature.

2.6.1.7.rationale: Kynurenine aminotransferase catalyzes a single transamination reaction; no evidence of a fused second catalytic domain was found.

2.7.1.147.rationale: ADP-dependent glucokinase is a single-activity sugar kinase (ADP-dependent kinase family found in archaea); no bifunctional/multifunctional fusion reported.

2.7.1.16.rationale: Ribulokinase is a single-activity carbohydrate kinase in arabinose/ribulose catabolism; literature search found no fused second catalytic activity.

2.7.1.25.rationale: In animals and fungi, APS kinase (EC 2.7.1.25) is fused with ATP sulfurylase (EC 2.7.7.4) into a single polypeptide, PAPS synthase (PAPSS), which carries both distinct catalytic activities needed to make PAPS from ATP and sulfate.

2.7.1.3.rationale: ATP:D-fructose 1-phosphotransferase (ketohexokinase/fructokinase) is a single-activity carbohydrate kinase; no fused second catalytic activity reported.

2.7.1.33.rationale: Pantothenate kinase (PanK/CoaA) itself is monofunctional; literature on the CoA pathway explicitly distinguishes PanK from the separate bifunctional phosphopantothenoylcysteine ligase/decarboxylase (PPCS-PPCDC) enzyme further down the pathway.

2.7.1.4.rationale: ATP:D-fructose 6-phosphotransferase (fructokinase) is a single-activity sugar kinase with no reported fused second catalytic domain.

2.7.4.21.rationale: Inositol hexakisphosphate kinase (IP6K) catalyzes a single phosphotransfer activity; a review on inositol phosphate kinase 'versatility' discusses multiple distinct kinase enzymes rather than a single fused multi-activity polypeptide.

2.7.7.48.rationale: In flaviviruses (Zika, dengue, West Nile, yellow fever), the RNA-directed RNA polymerase activity (EC 2.7.7.48) is fused in the same NS5 polypeptide with an N-terminal RNA cap methyltransferase domain (EC 2.1.1.56/2.1.1.57), two distinct catalytic activities in one protein; many other RNA viruses covered by this EC have standalone monofunctional RdRps, so confidence is medium rather than high.

2.7.7.6.rationale: DNA-directed RNA polymerase is catalytically a single-activity enzyme; bacterial/eukaryotic RNA polymerases are multi-subunit complexes of separate gene products rather than a single polypeptide fusing two distinct catalytic activities, so this does not meet the bifunctional bar.

2.7.7.7.rationale: Classic bacterial/family-A DNA polymerase I (e.g. E. coli, Taq, Mycobacterium) fuses three distinct catalytic activities into one polypeptide: 5'->3' polymerase (EC 2.7.7.7), 3'->5' proofreading exonuclease, and 5'->3' exonuclease (nick-translation/FEN); literature on domain dissection (e.g. S. pneumoniae Pol I lacking the 3'-5' exo domain, Mycobacterial Pol1's FEN/EXO-POL architecture) confirms these are separable, genuinely fused catalytic domains rather than moonlighting.

2.7.7.8.rationale: Polynucleotide phosphorylase (PNPase) is a single-activity phosphorolytic exoribonuclease/polymerase enzyme; it participates in multi-protein degradosome complexes with separate gene products (e.g. RNase E, RhlB), which is not the same as a fused second catalytic activity.

2.7.8.13.rationale: MraY (phospho-MurNAc-pentapeptide translocase) catalyzes a single phosphotransferase reaction in peptidoglycan lipid I synthesis; no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity.

2.8.3.1.rationale: Acetyl-CoA:propanoate CoA-transferase catalyzes a single CoA-transfer reaction; no literature describes a fused second catalytic activity.

2.8.3.8.rationale: Butanoyl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase (butyrate-acetoacetate CoA-transferase) is a single-activity CoA-transferase with no reported fused second catalytic activity.

3.1.1.17.rationale: Gluconolactonase (D-glucono-1,5-lactone lactonohydrolase) catalyzes a single hydrolysis reaction in the pentose phosphate/oxidative pathway; no fused second catalytic activity reported.

3.1.3.11.rationale: Standalone fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (FBPase-1, EC 3.1.3.11) is a distinct, unrelated enzyme from the bifunctional PFK-2/FBPase-2 (6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase, EC 2.7.1.105/3.1.3.46); searches targeting 3.1.3.11 specifically found no bifunctional fusion reports.

3.1.3.2.rationale: NADP+ 2'-phosphohydrolase activity overlaps with general acid phosphatase activity but is a single catalytic (hydrolase) function; no fused second catalytic activity reported.

3.1.3.27.rationale: Phosphatidylglycerophosphatase (PGP phosphatase) catalyzes a single dephosphorylation step in phospholipid biosynthesis; no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

3.1.3.4.rationale: Phosphatidate phosphatase (e.g. lipin) has a known moonlighting role as a transcriptional co-regulator in the nucleus, but that is a non-catalytic regulatory function, not a second fused catalytic activity, so it stays monofunctional per the moonlighting exclusion rule.

3.1.4.16.rationale: 2',3'-cyclic-nucleotide 3'-phosphodiesterase (CNPase) is associated with myelin structure, but that is a structural/localization role, not a second catalytic activity; only the single phosphodiesterase activity is catalytic.

3.1.4.37.rationale: 2',3'-cyclic-nucleotide 2'-phosphodiesterase catalyzes a single hydrolysis reaction; no literature reports a fused second catalytic activity.
